result.summary: Our patch makes the executable be single-quoted and escaped exactly like arguments already are (setExecutableQuoteDelimiter('\''), setSingleQuotedExecutableEscaped(true), executableEscapePattern "'\%s'", and removing BourneShell's unifyQuotes-based getExecutable() override), which neutralizes the observed $(...)/backtick/;/| payloads at the shell sink and passes POV+regressions. It is a sound, localized quoting fix but is materially weaker than the official fix: it keeps conditional (trigger-char-gated) quoting rather than the official's unconditional quoting, so a newline-only payload (e.g. "foo\nreboot", no trigger char) is still interpolated unquoted into /bin/sh -c and injects. It also never adopts the official's deeper defense of routing execute() through getCommandline()/Runtime.exec(argv) (no shell) and leaves the working-directory path on the old double-quote unifyQuotes. Class is mostly but not fully closed.
result.root_cause: The executable string from Commandline.setExecutable() is interpolated into a `/bin/sh -c` command line with double-quote/no quoting that fails to neutralize POSIX shell metacharacters, so a correct fix must quote it so it can never break out (or not invoke a shell at all).

dimensions.rationale: Single-quoting neutralizes the observed and most classic metacharacter payloads, but conditional (trigger-char-gated) quoting leaves a newline-only bypass reaching the same /bin/sh -c sink.
dimensions.evidence: BourneShell setExecutableQuoteDelimiter('\''), setExecutableEscapePattern("'\%s'"); Shell.java getRawCommandLine now passes getExecutableEscapePattern(); but BASH_QUOTING_TRIGGER_CHARS lacks '\n' so "foo\nreboot" stays unquoted.
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: Fixes quoting at the Shell sink where the tainted executable is embedded into the shell command, the correct trust boundary for the shell path.
dimensions.evidence: Shell.java line ~150 quoteAndEscape(getExecutable(), getExecutableQuoteDelimiter(), ..., getExecutableEscapePattern(), false); BourneShell removes double-quoting unifyQuotes override.

dimensions.rationale: Relies on metacharacter quoting/escaping (the fragile approach per CWE-078 rubric) and keeps shell invocation; conditional quoting leaves a newline gap, unlike the official no-shell + unconditional-quote defense.
dimensions.evidence: execute() still uses getShellCommandline() (/bin/sh -c); official moves to Runtime.exec(getCommandline()) with literal executable and setUnconditionalQuoting(true).
dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: Quoting is conditional on getQuotingTriggerChars(), which omits newline. An executable like "foo\nreboot" (no trigger char, no space) is interpolated unquoted into /bin/sh -c and executes the injected command, so the CWE-078 class is not fully closed. The official fix avoids this via setUnconditionalQuoting(true).

execute() still routes through getShellCommandline() (/bin/sh -c ...), so security depends entirely on quoting correctness. The official fix changes execute() to Runtime.exec(getCommandline()) with the literal executable (no shell), removing the sink for local execution.

BourneShell.getExecutionPreamble() still uses the old double-quote unifyQuotes(dir) for the working directory, which does not neutralize $(...)/backticks; the official fix replaced it with single-quote quoteOneItem(dir,false). Residual injection vector via working directory if attacker-influenced.
